src.note: The URL at the upload's intrinsic width. The srcset always lists the intrinsic width and nothing wider, so src is always that width (contract/image-sizes.json, srcset).

srcset.note: The candidate widths contract/image-sizes.json leaves for the sizes below, up to and including the upload's intrinsic width, and that width when it is no candidate, ascending, each '<url> <width>w'. The URLs are the platform's image pipeline's; the widths are the contract's (SC-016).

sizes.note: The default sizes of the image's slot (contract/image-sizes.json placements) for the band its section is drawn in, and for a card the grid's column count (SC-016). The site logo's is its drawn width in px (the logo slot's rule). A client site that swaps the view or changes the layout may declare its own, in salt-overrides.json.

loading.note: lazy, but eager on the header logo, which is above the fold (site-logo.json, SC-019). Never on the priority image, which is eager by default.

style.when: the parent passes a fit or a position (a section background does)
style.note: Fit is cover or contain. Position is the keyword pair for the nine positions (top left, top, top right, left, center, right, bottom left, bottom, bottom right), or, for focal-point, the image's stored focal point as <x>% <y>%; with no stored focal point the declaration is left out and the stylesheet's centre applies. The frame fill itself comes from the shared stylesheets (SC-011), so no inline fill is required; one a platform writes is redundant and harmless. No custom property carries the focal point: the stylesheets give way to this inline style.

root.note: The image takes the class its parent gives it (salt-hero__image, salt-gallery__image and so on); media has no class of its own. sizes and srcset are the image slot's default from contract/image-sizes.json. Always one img, never inside picture and never beside source elements (SC-007).

zeroState: Not drawn when the image does not resolve.

notes.text: Alt precedence is the parent's: an explicit alt, else the stored alt, else empty (decorative).

An image is one img with srcset, sizes, width and height, never picture (SC-007). Formats (WebP, AVIF) are negotiated by each platform's image pipeline behind the srcset URLs, not chosen in the markup. The priority image carries fetchpriority="high" and is never loading="lazy" (section#priority-media).

Width and height are always drawn, the image's intrinsic size, also when the stylesheet makes it fill its frame (SC-007): they give the browser the aspect ratio before the image loads. The "when not fill" condition 0.1.0 drafted goes.

owes: Write the inline style object-fit and object-position the parent passes, with focal-point as the image's stored focal point (Payload's upload focalPoint, as <x>% <y>%), left out when none is stored; objectPosition() maps focal-point to nothing today (components/image-sizes.ts).

Srcset capped at the upload's intrinsic width (SC-016): next/image lists every candidate the sizes leaves, 3840w included, whatever the upload's width. Salt for Next.js owes listing only the candidates at or below the intrinsic width, then the intrinsic width itself, and writing src as the URL at the intrinsic width.

Width and height on every image, fill images included (SC-007): next/image's fill mode writes neither, so the showcase and listing card images, the logo strip and the case study view's images draw none today. They are the upload's intrinsic size and give the aspect ratio before the image loads.
Drop x-image; take the parent's class; derive sizes from the same contexts.
Its picture_sources opt-in, which wraps the img in picture with source elements, is non-conforming (SC-007): drop it and negotiate formats in the image pipeline behind srcset.

Write the inline style object-fit and object-position when the parent passes a fit or a position: the nine positions as keyword pairs, and focal-point as the attachment's stored focal point as <x>% <y>%, left out when none is stored. It stores no focal point today, so focal-point draws the stylesheet's centre until it does.

Image sizes (SC-016): each image's sizes from its slot in contract/image-sizes.json for its section's band, written exactly: disable WordPress 6.7's auto-sizes, which prepends 'auto, ' to a lazy image's sizes (add_filter('wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes', '__return_false')). The srcset by exactly the contract's rule: filter wp_calculate_image_srcset to the table's candidate widths at or above the slot's floor (640 x the smallest bare vw share in its sizes / 100, or none), capped at the upload's intrinsic width, plus the intrinsic width (the full-size upload), dropping core's default sizes (300, 768, 1024, 1536) and any other registered size; register an uncropped image size for every candidate width so each exists, and raise max_srcset_image_width to the widest candidate. Worked examples from the fixtures: the carousel's fern-bed slide (card slot unbanded, sizes '(min-width: 64rem) 19rem, (min-width: 40rem) 50vw, 100vw', floor 320, an 800px upload) lists 384w, 640w, 750w, 800w; the full-bleed hero's background (full slot, sizes 100vw, floor 640, a 2400px upload) lists 640w, 750w, 828w, 1080w, 1200w, 1920w, 2048w, 2400w. src is the full-size upload.
